A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the effects of tissue nitrogen content on respiration rate are small and can be ignored when estimating annual maintenance respiration costs, but that tissue nitrogen content is a good predictor of basal respiration rate.
the effects of temperature on respiration rates are best expressed as a Q(10), while the effects of tissue nitrogen content are best expressed as an exponential function of tissue nitrogen content.
the respiration rates in stems and branches are a function of tissue nitrogen content, cambium temperature and the interaction of these two variables.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of temperature and tissue N on respiration are additive and that respiration is not a simple function of temperature alone.
the effects of temperature and tissue N on respiration are not independent, so it's important that both factors are considered in any model.
